resources.string: Welcome to Sommelle
Sommelle guides you for six to eight weeks towards better sleep, using the method recommended first for insomnia: cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I).
Each morning, you fill in your sleep diary. Each week, Sommelle adjusts your schedule.
Your data stays on your phone. No account, nothing is sent.
Sommelle does not replace medical advice.
Get started
A few questions first, to check that the program is right for you. It takes two to three minutes.
How old are you?
Under 18
65 and over
Next
Do you work nights or shifts?
For example, rotating shifts, or regular night shifts.
Are your nights mostly interrupted by someone else?
A baby, a relative who needs help at night…
Do you snore loudly, with pauses in breathing that someone has noticed?
Do you ever fall asleep without meaning to during the day?
In meetings, on public transport, or at the wheel.
Has a doctor told you that you have bipolar disorder?
Do you have epilepsy?
Are you pregnant?
Do you drive for work, or operate dangerous machinery?
Or a job where a moment of inattention could have serious consequences.
Would you prefer a program without reducing your time in bed?
This part of the program can increase daytime tiredness at first. Without it, the program is still useful, with a more gradual effect.
Do you go to bed and get up very late, but sleep well once you fall asleep?
Lately, have you been feeling at the end of your rope, or hopeless?
Your answer stays on your phone.
The full program is right for you
For one week, simply fill in your diary each morning. After that, Sommelle will suggest a sleep schedule, adjusted every week.
A program adapted for you
Based on your answers, Sommelle will not reduce your time in bed. You will follow the rest of the program: the diary, the advice for the night and the exercises.
Sommelle is not suited to your situation
Sommelle\'s method is designed for insomnia in adults. A doctor can offer you better-suited help.
Good to know
Start the program
Got it
Sommelle is designed for adults. Talk to your doctor about your sleep.
Snoring with pauses in breathing: talk to your doctor. It can be a sign of sleep apnea, which can be treated.
Falling asleep during the day: talk to your doctor. In the meantime, avoid driving if you feel drowsy.
Bipolar disorder: reducing time in bed can destabilize mood. Talk about your sleep with the doctor who follows you.
Epilepsy: lack of sleep can make seizures more likely. Talk about your sleep with the doctor who follows you.
Very late schedule: this may be a shift in your body clock rather than insomnia. A doctor can advise you.
Night or shift work: the standard program is not designed for this rhythm. An occupational health or sleep doctor can advise you.
In the first weeks, tiredness may increase. If you feel drowsy, do not drive or operate dangerous machinery.
When your nights are interrupted by someone else, the lack of sleep does not come from insomnia. Talk to your doctor if tiredness weighs on you.
During pregnancy, Sommelle will not reduce your time in bed.

If you are going through a hard time, please reach out now: call your local emergency number or a crisis line in your country, such as 988 in the United States. In France, 3114 is free, day and night, with trained people who listen.
Call 3114 (France)
